title: Localized consent banner states the required disclosures

claim.statement: The rendered consent banner text for each shipped locale states (1) what data is collected or why, (2) that third parties such as analytics or advertising partners receive it, and (3) how the visitor can refuse or withdraw consent.

question.instructions: The state is the visible text of a website consent banner in any language. Which option describes it?

criteria.A: it states the purpose of data collection, AND names third parties or partners who receive data, AND tells the visitor how to refuse or withdraw consent
criteria.B: it is a consent banner but at least one of those three disclosures is missing
criteria.C: it is not consent banner text

notes: Placeholder digests (all zeros) mark inputs that do not exist yet: the calibration set and the control fixtures. Replace them with real SHA-256 digests and a measured ECE before this rubric is frozen into a plan; a rubric with a placeholder digest must not back an assurance request.
Checkpoint is pinned to laya-multilingual; Router auto-selection is not used because a mostly-English banner would route to the English checkpoint and change the model under test per input.
measured_ece 0.106 is the published post-temperature figure for laya-multilingual, not a measurement on this rubric's calibration set.
Option C is deliberately in neither set: non-banner text maps to INCONCLUSIVE `answer_not_decisive`, which means the target locator is wrong, not that the claim failed.
This checks that disclosures are stated, not that the wording satisfies any particular law; legal sufficiency is out of scope for a System One rubric.
